title: Tutorial 01 – Crystal Structure and Energy Bands
text:
1 Learning objectives

Describe the crystal structure of silicon.
Explain how energy bands arise in a solid.
Distinguish metals, semiconductors, and insulators by their band gap.

title: Tutorial 01 – Crystal Structure and Energy Bands
text:
2 From atoms to energy bands
When many atoms come together in a lattice, their discrete energy levels broaden into bands. The gap between the top of the valence band and the bottom of the conduction band is the band gap, \(E_g\).

Animation: the atomic levels of N atoms split and merge into the valence and conduction bands.



Material
Band gap \(E_g\) at 300 K




Silicon (Si)
1.12 eV


Germanium (Ge)
0.66 eV


Gallium arsenide (GaAs)
1.42 eV

title: Tutorial 01 – Crystal Structure and Energy Bands
text:
3 Intrinsic carrier concentration
In an intrinsic semiconductor, electrons and holes are generated in pairs:
\[
n_i = \sqrt{N_c N_v}\, e^{-E_g / 2kT}
\]



Approximate \(n_i\) of silicon versus temperature (constant \(E_g = 1.12\) eV).

title: Tutorial 01 – Crystal Structure and Energy Bands
text:
4 Summary

Bands form because atomic levels split when atoms are brought together.
The band gap \(E_g\) decides whether a solid behaves as a metal, semiconductor, or insulator.
\(n_i\) grows exponentially with temperature.







NoteExercise



Why does \(n_i\) rise so quickly with temperature?

title: Tutorial 01 – Fundamental Antenna Parameters
text:
1 Learning objectives

Define radiation pattern, beamwidth, and directivity.
Relate gain to directivity and radiation efficiency.
Use the Friis equation for a simple link budget.

title: Tutorial 01 – Fundamental Antenna Parameters
text:
2 Radiation pattern, directivity, and gain
Directivity is the ratio of radiation intensity in a given direction to the average radiation intensity:
\[
D(\theta,\phi) = \frac{4\pi\, U(\theta,\phi)}{P_{\text{rad}}}
\]
Gain includes losses through the radiation efficiency \(e_r\):
\[
G = e_r \, D
\]



Normalized elevation pattern of a half-wave dipole.

title: Tutorial 01 – Fundamental Antenna Parameters
text:
3 Friis transmission equation
\[
P_r = P_t \, G_t \, G_r \left(\frac{\lambda}{4\pi R}\right)^2
\]






NoteExercise



A 2.4 GHz link has \(R = 100\) m, \(G_t = G_r = 5\) dBi, and \(P_t = 20\) dBm. Estimate \(P_r\).
